import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Stochastic_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 13  # destinations
    S = 12  # scenarios
    alpha = 0.9  # confidence level
    max_violations = int(math.floor((1 - alpha) * S))

    supplies = [145, 182, 134, 104, 157]
    recourse_caps = [58, 72, 53, 41, 62]
    base_costs = [[10.97, 7.52, 11.8, 22.29, 22.65, 22.16, 20.95, 17.26, 9.55, 21.62, 23.16, 16.56, 19.81], [19.57, 5.56, 7.38, 18.44, 21.05, 6.8, 10.2, 18.79, 23.92, 19.15, 6.41, 16.83, 6.17], [6.09, 16.96, 15.44, 7.8, 18.7, 21.79, 13.43, 14.63, 14.58, 17.23, 8.39, 11.07, 23.65], [6.2, 19.35, 22.84, 20.24, 18.28, 8.41, 19.15, 16.33, 17.11, 7.95, 11.59, 20.92, 5.36], [10.28, 17.66, 19.34, 21.93, 14.42, 17.65, 20.25, 8.0, 16.35, 8.49, 14.94, 13.16, 5.44]]
    recourse_costs = [[21.94, 15.04, 23.6, 44.58, 45.3, 44.32, 41.9, 34.52, 19.1, 43.24, 46.32, 33.12, 39.62], [39.14, 11.12, 14.76, 36.88, 42.1, 13.6, 20.4, 37.58, 47.84, 38.3, 12.82, 33.66, 12.34], [12.18, 33.92, 30.88, 15.6, 37.4, 43.58, 26.86, 29.26, 29.16, 34.46, 16.78, 22.14, 47.3], [12.4, 38.7, 45.68, 40.48, 36.56, 16.82, 38.3, 32.66, 34.22, 15.9, 23.18, 41.84, 10.72], [20.56, 35.32, 38.68, 43.86, 28.84, 35.3, 40.5, 16.0, 32.7, 16.98, 29.88, 26.32, 10.88]]
    demand_scenarios = [[26, 36, 34, 11, 21, 22, 14, 35, 22, 30, 43, 40, 53], [42, 39, 44, 7, 17, 21, 15, 45, 17, 46, 35, 48, 45], [30, 25, 28, 8, 22, 24, 16, 59, 16, 31, 36, 44, 52], [34, 38, 26, 12, 25, 28, 18, 35, 25, 42, 27, 49, 37], [27, 35, 29, 8, 22, 36, 14, 41, 17, 42, 42, 33, 40], [31, 39, 37, 8, 25, 29, 16, 51, 27, 46, 32, 30, 42], [32, 44, 27, 12, 17, 26, 11, 40, 22, 49, 48, 47, 48], [39, 27, 27, 11, 23, 20, 11, 44, 28, 34, 42, 46, 36], [32, 37, 40, 8, 25, 26, 17, 58, 18, 50, 42, 54, 47], [31, 44, 39, 11, 27, 25, 13, 46, 16, 33, 34, 42, 49], [30, 45, 38, 13, 19, 36, 15, 48, 16, 37, 28, 55, 49], [28, 41, 26, 11, 27, 36, 14, 44, 22, 49, 47, 35, 61]]

    # Big-M: largest demand * 2
    M = max(demand_scenarios[s][j] for s in range(S) for j in range(J)) * 2

    # --- Variables ---
    # Stage 1: base shipments
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Base_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Stage 2: recourse shipments per scenario
    y = {}
    for s in range(S):
        for i in range(I):
            for j in range(J):
                y[(i,j,s)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Recourse_S{i}_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # Violation indicators
    z = {}
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            z[(j,s)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Violate_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # --- Objective: minimize base cost + expected recourse cost ---
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(base_costs[i][j] * x[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J))
        + (1.0 / S) * quicksum(recourse_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j,s)]
                               for s in range(S) for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply (base)
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"SupplyBase_S{i}")

    # C2: Supply (recourse per scenario)
    for i in range(I):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(y[(i,j,s)] for j in range(J)) <= recourse_caps[i],
                name=f"SupplyRecourse_S{i}_Sc{s}")

    # C3: Demand chance constraint (SAA)
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(x[(i,j)] + y[(i,j,s)] for i in range(I))
                + M * z[(j,s)] >= demand_scenarios[s][j],
                name=f"DemandChance_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # C4: Violation budget per destination
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(z[(j,s)] for s in range(S)) <= max_violations,
            name=f"ViolationBudget_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Operations Leadership and Regional Logistics Managers
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: Today
Subject: Staged shipping plan under demand uncertainty with service reliability target

Challenge
Our stores face fluctuating customer demand across the network. Committing shipments too aggressively leads to excess inventory and carrying costs; committing too conservatively risks stockouts, lost sales, and emergency freight. We need a pragmatic plan that balances cost and service, recognizing that actual demand will vary from forecasted expectations.

Two-phase approach
- Base plan before demand is known: We will lock in an upfront shipping plan from warehouses to stores using forecast information. This plan must fit within available base inventory at each warehouse and reflect typical transport costs.
- Emergency adjustments after demand is known: Once actual demand is revealed, we will deploy targeted emergency shipments to close any gaps. These expedites carry higher per‑unit costs and must respect separate emergency capacity limits.

Reliability target
Our service posture requires that each store’s demand be fully satisfied in most forecast cases, as defined by the agreed confidence level. It is acceptable to fall short in a small share of cases, recognizing the trade‑off between cost and reliability. This ensures high customer satisfaction without routinely overspending to cover rare extremes.

Business goal
We will identify the most cost‑effective combination of base shipments and contingency actions that:
- Keeps base shipments within warehouse inventory availability, and emergency shipments within separate contingency capacity.
- Achieves the store‑level service reliability target across the forecast set.
- Delivers the lowest expected total cost, combining the committed base plan and the average emergency expenditure observed across the demand scenarios.

Operational guardrails and next steps
- Validate inputs: warehouse base supplies, emergency capacities, lane costs, and scenario demand profiles.
- Align on the reliability target and confirm it governs every store.
- Produce the base shipping plan that best positions inventory before demand is known.
- Define clear triggers for emergency activations and ensure contingency capacity is reserved accordingly.
- Monitor performance by comparing realized demand to the scenario set, tracking service and cost outcomes, and refreshing the plan as forecasts evolve.
